steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9 inch round cake pan.

Combine the rice flour, tapioca flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk together egg and buttermilk . Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and pour in the wet. Stir just until the dry ingredients are moistened. Pour into the cake pan.

Bake for 65 minutes in the preheated oven, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Cool on a wire rack, for 10 minutes before removing from the pan. Wrap bread in plastic wrap or aluminum foil and let stand overnight for the best flavor.

raw_recipe.headline: Gluten-Free Irish Soda Bread
raw_recipe.description: This recipe uses rice and tapioca flour instead of wheat and it still tastes yummy!

review.reviewBody: This recipe is wonderful. I am allergic to wheat and milk and so I just addapted the buttermilk to rice milk with 1 T vinegar. Most of the bread recipes that I have tried have turned out crumbly, but amazingly, this one is very nice and chewy. This will defenantly go in my recipe book! Like others have said, it needs to be about a total of 35 to 40 minutes cook time.

I made this and as suggested, used 1/4 sugar, and cut baking time to about 40 minutes. I added orange zest - 2 tsp, coconut flakes, about 1/4 cup and handful of dried cranberries. I would have used raisins, but didn’t have any. I am not gluten intolerant, but wanted to impress a friend who is. I impressed myself. It is absolutely delicious.

Sooo good! I used Pillsbury gluten free all purpose flower blend (with xanthan gum), and mixed 1 Tbs apple cider vinegar with milk in place of buttermilk. Also added 1 tsp cinnamon and cooked only 35 minutes. Turned out perfect. Will add to my favorites!

Very good and easy! Added 1/2 cup currants that I plumped in hot water. Pat dry and whisk into dry ingredients before adding wet. Baking time is only @ 35-40 mins! Do not bake for the 65 mins as recipe calls for or will be charcoal. Yummy!

I used 1 cup ground oatmeal, 1/2c. rice flour, 1/4 tapioca flour, and 1/4 cup finely ground flax seed for the flours. I used no sugar, but instead used 1 tablesppon real maple syrup, 1 tblspn. honey, and 2 tablespoons milk whey. I also added 1 teaspoon cardomen and a handful of raisens. This turned out so nice. Baked for about 35 minutes. Nice brown color, great texture and gently flavored.
I halved the sugar, mixed in 1/4 cup melted butter right before putting it in the pan, and cooked it in a round metal cake pan for 45 minutes. Delicious!

I like this bread. Very easy to make. I have just started on a no gluten diet due to an allergy to wheat. This was is my first try at backing gluten free. I am also dairy free so I substituted almond milk and lemon for the butter milk. I also melted some gluten free butter substitute and poured it over the top and sprinkled some gluten free oat bran on top. I also sifted the flours, backing soda, and baking powder, and salt together, before adding the egg and "milk". I hope it will toast up nice for breakfast with jelly. I will let you know. I think I will add some chopped walnuts, or some pumpkin seeds in it next time to add some more fiber.

I used brown rice flour instead of white and buckwheat flour instead of tapioca. Also used a bread tin to get the loaf shape! Like many others, I reduced the cooking time by about 20 mins. It is a nice, simple recipe and tastes good. Best of all it is guilt free as I have a wheat intolerance - so thanks!

yum! I didn't have rice flour so I substituted 1/2 cup flaxseed flour + 1/2 cup plantain flour + 1/2 cup quinoa flour. I also substituted the buttermilk with almond milk and 1/2 tsp of vinegar, and omitted the baking powder and added another 1/2 tsp baking soda because I have a corn allergy. It came out amazing!! It's more of a corn bread texture but still delicious. Very good recipe, will try it with rice flour next time but it's good to know that really any flours work in it!

This is awesome for gluten free. Nice texture and color. Being a novice at some of these grains, I bought sweet rice flour thinking it was probably the same as white rice flour. Wrong! I discovered the error, hunted about the pantry and found quinoa flour, high protein and high fiber. This substitution worked just fine, but I will do it correctly on my next pass. I really don't measure to the gram but this recipe is very forgiving.

I adore this bread! Tastes as good as any I've had in Ireland. I substitute brown rice syrup for sugar, and rice milk & apple cider vinegar for buttermilk. Best eaten fresh out of the oven, with stew or thick soup. This year I'm making it to use in stuffing for T-day. I predict it will be awesome.
Based on the reviews, I was really looking forward to a moist, delicious bread. From a visual perspective, the bread looked beautiful. However, it was very dry and crumbly.
Based on the reviews, I was really looking forward to a moist, delicious bread. From a visual perspective, the bread looked beautiful. However, it was very dry and crumbly.
I cooked it in bread pans for 45 minutes and it is perfectly golden brown and not as tough! It's delicious with coffee or just with butter and jam! I LOVE this recipe! :-)
I used just one small spoon of sugar and I have to say that this bread is really good. I specialy like that there is no yeast in it.

After making this a few months ago, I decided to tweak a few ingredients and now it tastes MUCH better! I substituted the white rice flour and tapioca flour with an all-purpose gluten-free flour (I use King Arthur Flour because it works the best in most of my gluten-free recipes); cut the sugar to 1/3 cup; cut the salt to 1/2 tsp; and added 1/2 cup of currants to the dry ingredients before adding the egg/buttermilk mixture. There were no other changes to the other ingredients. I baked it in a glass bread pan (greased with butter) at 400 deg F for 35 minutes. The higher temperature gives the soda bread a slightly crispier browned topping, and cooked the loaf evenly throughout. THIS version turned out pretty tasty!

It's great, I'd give it five stars for tasty gluten free easy make bread however this recipe calls for way too much sugar. First time I made it with 1/2 cup it was way too sweet. I did 1/4 cup the second time and it was much better. Will put a little less the next time too. Super bread with less sugar!

I made it today and it came out wonderful! Loved it! I only added a tablespoon of apple vinegar and about 1/4 cup crushed cashew. Fluffy and delicious! Thanks so much for this wonderful recipe!

I was amazed that it didn't need any type of oil? Great!
Great recipe! I added some currants. My GF daughter really enjoyed this bread with honey.
I made this for my son- he loved it! Only used 2 Tbsp sugar and it was plenty sweet. Also baked for 45 min.
